# Check of M0-c-01 — the flat fixture and the S3 slice as data (closing round after fix round 1; lane `check/M0-c-01-close-r1`, flow flow-7, stage group 9, 2026-10-05)

Lane `check/M0-c-01-close-r1` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux
x64, Node 24.12.0) on 2026-10-05 from about 12:39 to 13:25. This seat is an implementer-side independent closing
checker. It is not the item's author (`build/M0-c-01`, L-0167), not its fixer (`build/M0-c-01-fix1`, L-0172), and
not its first checker (`check/M0-c-01`, L-0171). Under J162 and J169 the item's second check closes it. The seat
changed no file of the item and ran no git command. It ran one vitest process at a time: `--maxWorkers=2` for the
gates and `--maxWorkers=1` for every probe and mutant, with no `--` before a vitest flag (J182). `free -m` showed
9.6–12 GB available before each run. The probes and mutants ran in this seat's own scratch mirror
(`maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-c-01/close-r1/plat`). The mirror was copied from the tree at 12:40 and installed with
`--frozen-lockfile --offline`. Its `@plat/*` links resolve inside the mirror. Its `node_modules` was deleted
afterwards. Each mutated file was restored after its run and byte-compared (`cmp`) with the tree. The seat planned its
probes and mutants from the first check's failing lines, C-0204 and its own reading of the code. It did not read the
author's or the fixer's self-check folders, and it did not use their CHECKPOINT notes as a map.

## Verdict: PASS — B-1 and B-2 are fixed; no new blocker

Fix round 1 changed one source line. `pickCandidates` in `gates.ts` now keeps only the land inside ends of the pick
contour's crossings (`interior[u] === 1 && water[u] === 0`). The round also added a two-layout river test to
`picks.test.ts`, two F-WALL fixtures to `fwall.test.ts`, and choices row C-0204. The first check's evidence for both
blockers now comes out clean, and every mutant aimed at the two promises is killed (CONFIRMED). The fix does not
include one assertion the first check asked for: that no gate's inside node is water. Instead, C-0204 (2) records the
bridgehead gate as an open case and pins it in a test. This check accepts that as a declared choice. Its reasoning is
in note N-13 and summarized below.

## (3) New findings — none is a blocker

The fix changed no listed interface and no listed test id. Its source change is one filter, declared in C-0204 (1),
and its tests are additions. A grep of the owned files for `TODO`, `FIXME`, `.skip`, `.only` and `it.todo` finds
nothing. No path lies outside `plat/`. The fixer's CLEAN-ROOM row L-0172 exists and lists only rule-1 sources.

* **The bridgehead gate (note N-13, PLAUSIBLE as a design reading, CONFIRMED as measured).** The first check's B-1
  change asked the river test to assert that no gate's inside node is water. The fixer did not add that assertion.
  C-0204 (2) records the bridgehead gate as an open case instead, and the test pins it (exactly one bridgehead gate on
  seed 25, none on seed 21). This check's sweep found 6 bridgehead gates in 460 layouts. In 3 of them the gate point
  lies inside the water face, up to 12.40 m into a 40 m band with a 25 m spacing (probe R4). That matches C-0204 (2)'s
  "within half a spacing of the bank". It is not a wrong result under §4.2 S3 (7) and C-0017: the gate is the first
  point at T = t₁ on its route, which is the contour's own crossing. The stage-1 selection reaches over the river only
  through C-0201 (8)'s water reach, which the first check accepted. §4.2 S3 (4) adds water gates "where the river
  crosses the boundary", and how they meet this main gate is the trace's question (M0-c-02, M0-e-06). The deviation
  is declared, with a test, as J156 requires. It goes to the notes for M0-e-06.
* **The status of earlier notes (N-14).** N-9 is closed by the cap fixture (X06 and X07 killed). N-3 gains evidence:
  all 460 river layouts gave one ring.

Both are appended to `checks/M0-c-01-notes.md` as N-13 and N-14, recorded under
`landed/check-M0-c-01-notes.json`.

## Round 1 (lane `check/M0-c-01`), kept unchanged below

# Check of M0-c-01 (the flat fixture and the S3 slice as data) — first check

Lane `check/M0-c-01`. The checker is Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux x64,
Node 24.12.0). The item is in flow `flow-7`, stage group 9. This seat is an implementer-side independent checker and
not the item's author (`build/M0-c-01`, L-0167). No git command was run. Vitest ran one process at a time:
`--maxWorkers=2` for the gates and `--maxWorkers=1` for every mutant and probe, with no `--` before a vitest flag
(J182). `free -m` showed 7.5–9.7 GB available before each run. The mutants and probes ran in a scratch mirror of `plat/`
under `/home/cstokes111/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-c-01/mirror`. The mirror was rsynced from the tree at 06:55 and
installed with `--frozen-lockfile --offline`. Its `@plat/kernel` resolves inside the mirror and has no link to Maps. Its
`node_modules` was deleted afterwards. Nothing ran in the tree or in the author's self-check folder. The probes and the
40 + 1 targeted mutants were planned from the brief and the code before any of the author's self-check lines were used.

## Verdict: FAIL — two blockers

The slice is well built and well tested where it is pinned. Every gate passes within scope. Every listed interface and
listed test exists. The exit bar holds on 23 flat-fixture seeds. 36 of the 41 targeted mutants are killed. Two findings
are blockers:

| # | line | evidence | required change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B-1** | A wrong result on an input the slice accepts and C-0201 (8) claims to handle: on a site with a river, gate picks land **in the river**. `pickCandidates` takes the inside end of every crossed contour edge. The pick contour's selection includes the water that `spreadOverWater` reaches (C-0201 (8)), so water nodes become candidates. A pick on a water node is not reachable by the plaza tree, so its route is `unserved` with count 0 and the town gets N − 1 main gates with no F-WALL or F-ROUTE cause. | Probe P7 (mirror, `smallSite`-shaped `flatFixture(seed, { frameAreaHa: 400, walledHa: 30, water })`, a 40 m band at x0 with one deck, `requestedN: 3`): `"seed 21 x0 10000 deck 20000: candidates 73 wet 27; … unserved ordinals 1"`, `"seed 25 x0 20000 deck 0: candidates 69 wet 12; … unserved ordinals 1"`. Probe P5 audit: `"river 21 x0 10000 deck 20000: gates 2 != n 3; rungs [] unserved [{"ordinal":1,"code":"unserved","count":0,…}]"` and the same on 4 more river layouts. The author's own river test (`levelset.test.ts`, seed 21, deck at y 0) passes only because none of its 14 wet candidates wins a pick. §4.2 S3 (4) puts picks on the pick contour of stage 1's **land**, and "a river takes water gates, not this reduction". M0-e-06 runs this slice on a river. | Restrict the pick candidates to land nodes: interior nodes with `lattice.water === 0`, the inside ends of the contour's land crossings. Add a test on a river site whose pick contour crosses the river, for example seed 21 with the deck at y = 20 000 and `requestedN: 3`. It asserts that no pick and no gate's inside node lies on water, that `report.unserved` is empty and that `gates.length === n`. |
| **B-2** | F-WALL's "re-drawn from its **next** candidate" (§4.2 S3 (7); C-0201 (6): "the next in the pick's score order"; the title of `fwall.test.ts`'s second test) has no test that can fail. Every fwall fixture's ranked list holds at most two distinct nodes, with the alternative last, so a re-draw from any other position of the list passes. | Mutant **K26** (`slice.ts`: `const to = p.ranked[tried + 1]` → `p.ranked[p.ranked.length - 1 - tried]`): **survived**, `Tests 83 passed (83)` on `packages/layout/test/siting`. The change is not equivalent. Probe P9, with picks `[a]` and `[a, a, c, d]`: the original re-draws `[["redraw",1,4131],["redraw",2,3314]]` (to a, then to c); the mutant re-draws `[["redraw",1,3393]]` (straight to d). | Add an fwall fixture whose later pick ranks at least three distinct nodes and whose first re-draw candidate still coincides, for example ranked `[a, a, c, d]`. Assert the rungs exactly: `redraw` attempt 1 to `a`, then `redraw` attempt 2 to `c`, with the final pick `c`. Optional, because the change is equivalent on drawn picks (see N-9): also give a fixture more than four coinciding ranked entries, so that `GATE_REDRAWS` itself, rather than the list's length, caps the re-draws at 3. |

Every other finding is minor. Each is written to `checks/M0-c-01-notes.md` (N-1 – N-12) for M4.
